Thanks for pulling this together, Camila. Quick product context:
- PenguinAI indicated in discovery they will serve a mixture of chat prompts and completion endpoints. Likely model: rwin-1 / rwin-1-4k (decoder-only variant). If they want lower-latency/lower-cost during spikes, we can route to rwin-2-lite (reduced context, ~15% lower memory, small quality delta).
- Confirmed median tokens ~230, 95th percentile ~680 — consistent with Jenny's file. That token distribution matters for GPU slot sizing.

Recommendations:
- Allow the temporary uplift but require a staged fallback: 100% -> 75% -> 50% -> 25% traffic routing to rwin-2-lite if token-rate per GPU crosses the threshold.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for any repeated prompts; this can shave 20-30% of per-token compute in common patterns (we should offer this as an opt-in config).
- If they accept, we should pre-register rwin-2-lite as the fallback so routing is automatic.

Open question: does Sales want to charge for the uplift (Priyom)? If not, we should at least tie the uplift to a post-launch cost-recovery plan.

-Karthik

We can support the temporary uplift with caveats. Summary of what infra can commit:

- Lead time: need final confirmation by 2026-10-12 EOD to reserve burst instances and schedule on-call staff.
- Limits: we will enforce a token-throughput safeguard. If aggregate token/s per GPU exceeds safe limits for more than 10 minutes, auto-fallback to rwin-2-lite will be triggered.

Attachments: quota_change_template.pdf, capacity-plan.csv

Technical checklist for runbook (suggested):
1) Canary ramps and SLA measurement hooks (latency, 5xx rate, GPU utilization)
2) Fallback routing pre-registered to rwin-2-lite (must be approved by product)
3) Billing & legal check (if uplift > baseline, flag for sales to invoice or credit)
